## Versioning & stability

* The API is **path-versioned** (`/api/v1`). When it reaches general
 availability, breaking chan
ges will require a new version path.\n* **During the preview**, breaking changes to v1 may still happen; we'll note\n them in the
[changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changelog/overview.md).\n* **Additive changes** — new endpoints, new optional request fields,
new\n response fields, new error codes — are considered non-breaking and can ship\n at any time. Write clients that ignore unkn

own fields.
* Error **codes** are stable identifiers; error **messages** are not.

### Renamed surfaces

Three nouns this API
used are now what the product calls them: `scenario` is\n**study**, `journey` is **goal**, and `wave` is **swarm run**. The paths

, the
operation names, the SDK types and the noun-bearing response fields all moved:

| Was | Is |
| - | - |
| `/projects/{pr
ojectId}/scenarios[/{scenarioId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies[/{studyId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/user-testing/scenario
s/{scenarioId}/…` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies/{studyId}/…` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/scenario`
| `.../environments/{environmentId}/study` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys[/{journeyId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/goals[/{g
oalId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journey-runs/{runId}` | `/projects/{projectId}/goal-runs/{runId}` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}
/journeys-overview`, `.../journey-findings` | `.../goals-overview`, `.../goal-findings` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/waves/{waveId}
/insights` | `/projects/{projectId}/swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` |\n\nResponse fields followed their nouns: `scenarioId` → `s

tudyId`, `journeyId` →
`goalId`, `waveId` → `swarmRunId`, and `sessionsPerTarget` → `iterations`.

Two reads became one: `get_s
cenario` served the execution settings and\n`get_user_testing_scenario` served the environment id and the insights\nenvelope. `get

_study` returns both, and the two caller-dependent fields are
absent rather than null when you may not have them.

**Every old
path still works** and is unchanged, including its old response\nspellings. Each one answers with `Deprecation: true` and a `Link`
header naming\nits successor. They are undocumented on purpose — the spec is what a new\nintegration reads — and they are removed

at general availability.

A handful of operations kept their names through the rename and so have no
deprecated twin to hold t
he old field spellings. `get_swarms_overview`,\n`create_swarm` and `update_swarm` emit both and accept either — never both in\none

request — until general availability.

### Vocabulary

A name can move behind an alias; a VALUE cannot. `sourceType` is one f
ield with\none string in it, and a client switching on `\"scenario\"` has no second name to\nfall back to. So the values negotiate

.

Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the renamed values read canonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Vocabulary 2 |
| - |
- | - |\n| session `sourceType` | `scenario` | `study` |\n| session `parentRef.kind` | `scenario`, `journeyRun` | `study`, `goalRu
n` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`, `journeyRunId`, `journeyRefId` | `studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRefId` |\n| share `r

esourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scenario` | `study` |
| trace-destination `sourceTypes` | `scenario` | `study` |

Abse
nt means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today's contract. Any other value is a\n`400`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may name
a filter or a path segment\nby either spelling; a vocabulary-1 request may use only the legacy one, because\na boundary that acce
pts a spelling it does not announce is one two\nimplementations can disagree about. A response that varies by vocabulary sends\n`V

ary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary`.

This is a **separate header** from `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`, which is
eval-scoped by name and
moves on its own schedule. A deployment may speak one\nand not the other, so read\n`GET /projects/{projectId}/capabilities` — `ap
iVocabulary` and `vocabulary` are\ntwo blocks — before sending either. With the SDK:\n`new PlatformApiClient({ …, apiVocabulary: 2
e: `study` and\n`goal_run` are the canonical keys, `user_testing_scenario` and `journey_run`\nstill resolve to the same routes, an
d which one a response carries follows the\nOPERATION rather than the header — a renamed operation derives the canonical\nkey, its

deprecated twin the old one. `capabilities.apiVocabulary.resourceTypes`
lists both.

### Browser tools on chat sessions

> [
!NOTE]\n>\n> Hosted browser availability depends on the account and deployment. The browser workspace must be enabled to open the
live pane in the Playground.\n\n`POST /chat-sessions/messages` accepts an optional `browser: { policy?, profileId? }`. Attach it o
n every turn that should browse. The initial grant and profile are fixed; the current host policy and pinned read-only mode can na
rrow the effective permissions. Responses and traces include the read-only `chatSessionId`, browser metadata, and screenshot URLs

without inline image data.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| - | - | - |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/browser` | Create an empty API
session and its browser with `projectId`, `policy`, optional `profileId`, and a stable `idempotencyKey`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessio
ns/{sessionId}/browser/open` | Open or wake the session browser. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/command` | Execut
e a browser command under the session policy with a stable `commandId`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/note` | Ap
pend a command-ledger note. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/trace` | Read command receipts and screenshot evidence
. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/artifact` | Resolve a command screenshot URL. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessi
onId}/browser/close` | Release the session desktop. |\n\nOnly the owning user can drive an API session's browser. All inputs use t
he public `sessionId`; conversation and browser identifiers in responses are informational. Capacity refusals before execution rel
ease the turn lease so the same idempotency key can be retried. An execution with an unknown outcome must be inspected before atte

mpting a new action.

atform.> ## Documentation Index\n> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.mcpjam.com/llms.txt\n> Use this file to

discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Local Evals

> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine with m

cpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity

> [!NOTE]
>
> The upcoming SDK 10, CLI 6, and Vitest 0.3 releases requir
e an MCPJam login or `sk_` API key for every eval, including BYOK runs with uploads disabled. These versions must ship after the b
ackend run-start endpoint is deployed. Earlier versions keep their existing behavior.\n\n`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite
file locally: it connects your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model, grades the transcript with the same asser
tions a hosted run uses, and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your own provider key and authenticate the run wi
th MCPJam. With MCPJam-hosted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.\n\nResults are **never uploaded**. The comman
d writes results to your terminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It records the run start with MCPJam. Like every command, it
sends the CLI's single anonymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/telemetry.md) event, which `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TR

ACK=1` turns off; the run adds no telemetry of its own.

Run `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or
